experiment: Role transfer vs state/memory transfer ablation
execution: Executed twice locally; raw CSV and JSON summary byte-identical across runs.
key_findings: Role transfer improves held-out reachability relative to no transfer in tested damage settings.
Role plus state transfer has higher held-out reachability than role-only in all 18 aggregate configurations in this simulation.
State-copy accuracy is 100% by construction for modes that copy the categorical state; this is not evidence that meaningful memory can be transferred.
caveats: Categorical state is synthetic and copied exactly; no semantic memory or state reconstruction is modeled.
Held-out pairs are distinct from training pairs, but task-aware selection uses training pairs.

The local execution harness and committed reproduction script were independently authored versions and are not byte-identical; the repository script should be rerun to validate its own outputs before treating these hashes as its hashes.
